evals.prompt: Install the secret guard's home layer on this machine so every repo, including ones that never installed anything, is guarded against a credential value reaching a transcript.
evals.expected_output: The engine (secret_redact.py, secret-scan, redact-view) and the read-path hook land under the home layer, all executable where required, with a version stamp written. settings.json gets the PreToolUse hook and the deny rules. verify-secret-guard.sh --json reports every engine/guard/wiring check as pass and 0 failed. A second run leaves the tree clean.

evals.prompt: Install the secret guard's home layer where one payload file has already been hand-edited.
evals.expected_output: Without --adopt the installer refuses (exit 3), leaves the hand-edited file untouched, still installs the files that do not diverge, and makes no backup yet. With --adopt it backs up the previous copy, replaces it with the byte-identical shipped payload, and preserves the unrelated hook and keys already present in settings.json.

evals.prompt: Wire this repo's AGENTS.md to route credential reads through the secret guard and scaffold its repo-level pattern-additions file.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md gets exactly one secret-guard managed block and its pre-existing prose survives untouched. .agents/secret-guard.json is scaffolded with paths/safe_keys. A second run is a no-op (git status stays clean).
The installer refuses because there is no AGENTS.md, names initial-project as the fix, and fabricates neither AGENTS.md nor .agents/secret-guard.json.

evals.prompt: Read this dotenv-style config through the guard's engine and confirm the credential is detected and masked.
evals.expected_output: secret-scan exits 0 (found) and names a rule; redact-view masks the password behind a sha256 fingerprint and leaves the surrounding keys intact. The planted value never appears in either tool's output.

evals.prompt: Read this appsettings.json, whose password is embedded inside a connection-string value under an innocuous key name, through the guard's engine.
evals.expected_output: secret-scan still detects the credential even though no key in the document looks secret by name; redact-view masks it while leaving the surrounding structure and unrelated values intact. The planted value never appears in either tool's output.

evals.prompt: Read this ordinary config through the guard's engine and confirm it is left alone.
evals.expected_output: secret-scan reports clean (exit 1, no findings printed) and redact-view passes the file through byte-identical.
